```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A's demand evidence comes from the people who would pay. Solo therapists on r/therapists and in aggregated practice interviews complain about price and paying for unused features. B's demand evidence comes from end users, a competitor executive and one fraud anecdote, none of whom are the platform buyer B would sell to.",
    "A's buyer is a single practice owner paying a monthly subscription as a business expense, which fits a 90-day path to a first paying customer. B's brief says the bank channel needs 6–18 month sales cycles and SOC 2 Type II before outbound. Both are incompatible with the deadline.",
    "A has a sourced price anchor (TherapyNotes $69/mo, SimplePractice $49–99/mo with annual price increases after the PE acquisition) and a sourced switching motive. B's reachable self-serve segment already has free tiers (useHUMA free up to 1,000 verifications/mo; not.bot from $9.99/mo), which the brief itself says pushes pricing toward zero.",
    "A has a free, already-active channel where buyers compare EHRs (r/therapists), though self-promotion norms limit it. B's only near-term channel is a Product Hunt-style developer launch, and the brief offers no evidence that small dating apps or marketplaces would pay for it.",
    "Both carry regulatory weight. A's HIPAA burden is quantified ($8k–$25k year one) and is a known, bounded cost. B's biometric exposure (BIPA, bans or investigations of Worldcoin in Spain, Thailand and Colombia) is open-ended and depends on design, as B's own open questions acknowledge.",
    "A still has real weaknesses. The category is saturated. No sourced complaint asks specifically for a minimal notes-plus-reminders product. HIPAA overhead strains a six-week solo build. A wins on payer clarity and sales-cycle fit, not on strength of opportunity."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's quote from Trevor Traina, Chief Business Officer of Tools for Humanity, cited as demand evidence. It is marketing language from a direct competitor announcing its own Zoom deal, not a statement from any prospective buyer. It shows no willingness to pay among the small platforms B could actually reach in 90 days.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs make strong cases against their own ideas. A wins mainly because B's evidence shows its paying segments are either unreachable within 90 days or already served by free tiers. A's own unaddressed risks are significant: the HIPAA compliance cost and timeline, and no direct evidence of demand for a stripped-down product. A could also plausibly fail to land a paying customer in 90 days."
}
```
